title: Great app…. Horrible price
body: It’s a very well designed app however it is ridiculously expensive, £10 a month or £70 a year!!!! Way to expensive for something that other free apps can do 90% of what this one can
author: Zavier Jenkins

title: Half and half
body:
Downloaded it because I know the book and author. I love the look and feel especially how you have to describe each habit- which gives it purpose and meaning.
On the other hand, I didn’t realise it would come with a hefty subscription. Honestly I wasn’t expecting it until one day it popped up on my screen that I had a couple of days left on the trial. This put me off using it- I guess I felt that I couldn’t track habits long term and for me, that’s what’s important. Additionally, I had gotten so invested in using the app, it felt like a let down.
So @the publisher- please make it clear for everyone that they will have to pay and make the price reasonable- today we already have a high cost of living, we simply can’t justify spending so much for this app when there are many other alternatives.

body: Downloaded this after reading the book which was fantastic. In the beginning the app lived up to the standard of the book with a brilliant UI, really like the feedback when completing a habit and the tips you get that is reflected in the book. Although having a cap of 1 habit in the free version is ridiculous. Then being also capped at 6 habits with the paid version, which at the discounted rate is nearly £6 a month which is fairly heavy price to be paying for a habit tracker let alone being capped to only be able to create 6 habits. Uncapping the number of habits alone would bring this to 4 stars for me. For now I’ll be looking elsewhere for a good habit tracker.

author: Elijah 0631

title: Use a Google Sheet instead
body: Prefacing this review with the fact I’m a huge fan of James Clear’s work, this is just an honest review of this app: I love the idea of tracking habits - building a streak massively helps me with accountability, something this app has highlighted to me. But now the free month has passed I think it’s massively overpaid (£70/year) to essentially press a button to track a habit… it inspired me to set up a Google Sheet to track my habits for free this way instead. Also the analytics on the app weren’t very good, aesthetic or useful; it always took me too long to find what I was looking for. Unless you’re just wanting to track 1 habit (which you can do for free) don’t bother with this app. Love ya James.

author: WaanaMC

title: This app [actually] changed my life! But…
body:
I have been using this app for the past… 4 months or so? I love it! It’s changed my life for the better, big time. It is simple to use and has a beautiful and elegant interface. I’ve felt invested enough to purchase their yearly subscription pretty early on, within weeks of the app’s original launch date. 

That being said, there is a “but”, unfortunately…

I woke up today to find the app has randomly decided to wipe out over a week’s worth of log history for all 6 habits I’m tracking.

This happened weeks back with one sole habit, I was bummed but didn’t do much about it as it wasn’t a habit I was really that worried about.

Today’s issue was a low blow for me, however, as seeing one’s clean streak grow is paramount to keeping you inspired to be persistent.

Anyhow… considering the price of its yearly subscription, this bug/issue is simply unacceptable.

I’ve just contacted support. Waiting to hear back.

author: Ash Sobhani

title: Disappointing and overpriced
body:
It has a nice and well-considered design that's let down by a lack of basic features like dark mode and 24 hour time. It has a baffling need to be connected to the internet all the time to do basic tasks, so if you live in a city with patchy cell service like I do you're going to have a rough time. It also means the privacy of this app is a lot worse than it needs to be.

I was willing to try it for a month, especially given the fact that other habit tracking apps aren't as carefully designed or geared towards self-actualisation goals like this is but the asking price is very out of line for what it is. It's a well designed app, but it's not complex at all.

author: Jmanley

title: Good but not great
body: After reading the book and making a plan for myself to start/stop some habits, I was excited to see this. It works well for some habits, but it’s frustratingly not well set up for others - for example you have to specific which days of the week you’ll do something, which doesn’t work well for something you just want to do once or twice a week (on any day). And it doesn’t offer a way to track commitment devices. For example, every time I eat sugar I’ll donate £1 to charity. You’d have to log this again as a habit you commit to every day, which would show as failure if you didn’t then do it, rather than success! But will see how I get on. Hope this feedback is taken onboard as it would be great to see those changes.
author: Chalhay

title: High costs for app
body:

author: Scr00b!usPip

title: Great but expensive
body:
Really great habit tracker that I wouldn’t have thought of writing a review for but am doing so.

It really really helped form habits and the design is clean and the methods are scientific and the advices are so useful.

However, I had to sadly delete the app as it’s too expensive for me. I used the free trial for a month. I’ve since started copying over the techniques of implementation and design for myself as a free alternative (as it’s not something I’m looking to spend a dollar on) after having read the book - which I recommend (atomic habits) - and from the app, to my notes on phone.

title: Mixed feelings - app is nice enough but not worth the price
body: I have been using this app for a few months now and it has helped me develop some healthy habits from scratch. For example - I strength train, eat a portion of berries, and do some deep breathing every day (I did none of these before the app). These habits have really stuck and the psychology of the app is great for this - little habits, you can miss a day but not two (so it's not all or nothing), you get nice visual and tactile feedback to get the little dopamine hit. That said - this is really all the app offers and there are other apps that provide similar. This app is not as great as it appears to think it is when compared with other similar apps. The streaks app, for example, offers a lot of this functionality for free. I am very happy to pay for apps and I do not think that app developers should work hard and not get paid what they're worth. But the price feels ludicrous - and there are no staggered price points. I feel the team must surely lose money from this. There are many people who would gladly pay a smaller amount but who will not pay this. I actually did pay for a while but when considering my available budget I ended up cancelling my monthly subscription even though I would have continued it if it was cheaper. It also feels a little buggy especially since the recent display update. The haptic feedback seems hit and miss when completing a habit. I also liked the previous floating circles. The order of the habits seems to change haphazardly. I liked the repeatability of the old style which reinforced the repetitive nature of the habits. TLDR - the app is good and nice to use but it is mooching off the brand awareness imo. It is not as good as it thinks it is. The price point is crazy and the functionality doesn't justify it imo.
author: helen1351

title: Good but not worth subscribing (yet) imo
body:
It’s been a helpful app so far but essentially its just a daily to-do list which can be achieved using a calendar app or bullet journal. Hopefully we see some improvements in the future. Here’s what I’d love to see:

1. If I write the same identity for 2 or more habits, it doesn’t recognise that it’s the same identity. So the votes don’t add up and in the reflections section, the same identity is listed multiple times. Very surprising to see this. Surely it’s expected that we may have to develop multiple new habits to form our identity? So I’d love to see a way we can link our habits to existing identities.

2. We can only log day/time based identities. No mention of habit stacking or any of the other great concepts from the book! E.g. if I want to become a tidier person, I might want to put away laundry as soon as it’s ready to be put away, but this won’t always be the same day/time. 

3. The replace a bad habit option isn’t any different to creating a new habit so I don’t understand the purpose of this. The sentence structure is exactly the same. Also, as I mentioned in point 2, replacing a bad habit might not always be day/time based, as they’re dependent on other conditions. It could be ‘whenever I feel like having an unhealthy snack’ or ‘any time I need to travel anywhere X miles or less, I will walk instead’.

4. Looking at the free version and subscription comparison table, a maximum of 6 habits can be created which isn’t enough. It would be good to unlock more habits if we achieve a level of votes. A good way to gamify the app.

author: Nibras I

title: Good App, unjustifiably expensive
body:
The app is good but it’s honestly not much better than any other habit tracking app out there. The interface is simple and clean, I like the integration of the principles from atomic habits, albeit they are only basic and not inclusive of all the principles (yet?). 

There is a cap of 6 habits for the paid version which is probably reasonable. Only allowing one habit for the free version makes the app almost redundant. 

The price tag on this is where it really goes downhill. I don’t know how £20/month can be justified for such a simple app. I don’t know exactly what else is meant to be included other than the daily lessons from James but if you’ve read the book then I really can’t see how it adds that much more value. 

Comparable apps on the market are a quarter of this price for premium access. If it were around that price I would certainly consider purchasing the pro version. The price point it is at currently is absurd.

body:

It feels like James’ goal is first to make money and then help people stick to their habits. There is nothing wrong with that, but it’s not for me.

Other than that, the UI is easy to understand and you can get going pretty fast and the user experience is nice as well. However, due to the high subscription price, I will be uninstalling it.

title: Brilliant idea but too expensive for me
body:
This is brilliant, clear and easy to use but when I saw the price to continue using all the features after a 28 day free trial I was shocked. 
Maybe some will find it so beneficial they’ll pay the £17.99 a month or £119.99 a year but sadly it’s not possible for me. 
With your huge following I’d have hoped for a much lower price point, safe in the knowledge you’d easily have tens of thousands of raving fans willing to subscribe.

author: MG121226

title: Great app for supporting you in developing good habits
body:
Fabulous - Worth having!!!! Been by it for about a month. It works well for me, I’m actually properly acquiring one good habit now, and working towards a second one too. 
Thank you James!!!

My only reservation is the price: for those whose finances are a bit tight, the yearly fee would be ok if it wasn’t to be paid all upfront but in monthly instalments (there is an option to subscribe for a month at a time, but it is substantially costlier).

However, with a modicum of willpower and having the Atomic Book at hand, it is still possible to make effective use of the free version of the app, even though it is fairly constrained in comparison with the paying one.

In conclusion: definitely a great app!
author: grand midget

title: Awesome - can’t wait to see more of this app
body: The UI is beautiful, the onboarding is well put together and the information is golden as always from James Clear. The only reason I didn’t rate 5 stars is because I can only add one habit when first downloading the app. I have been following James for some time and have re-read atomic habits several times in that period - so I have multiple habits I want to keep of track of already. Let me add more - then it will be 5 stars. The functionality makes sense for beginners, but it should be able to be overridden.
author: kiewif

title: Simple. Effective.
body: A great compliment to the book Atomic Habits. Good first version of the app.
author: m@thereviewer

title: Easy to download and use immediately
body:
I have been waiting for this app for ages. Unlike others who were too impatient and downloaded it before it was glitch free I waited until notified that it was ready. 
You start with 1 habit a day and the more you record that you’ve completed that habit daily then you progress to a second habit. This means that our initial eagerness to log a multitude of habits we want to incorporate into our lives doesn’t then wane to log nothing at all. Such a fantastic idea. Thank you so much James Clear and your tech team.
author: Smarti64

title: Better than most, still could be better…
body:
I personally love the app compared to most with its simplicity and ease. I like that it’s very minimalist. However I don’t like that you can only start 1 habit at once mine was to read 20 pages a day but that doesn’t effect my habit of working out every day which I wanted to also create, because some habits are easier then others and it should be each user’s judgement to make on how many habits they start with i think you should change it to 3 habits are allowed then every 1/2 weeks you can add another 3 and add a multiplier so then the next 3 you have to wait a month, then for another 3 wait two months so by the time of (0 days + 2 weeks + 1 month + 2 months) 3 1/2 months you can have 12 habits all steadily running.

If you don’t do this please just add at least another 2 to both 👍

author: Pinnityhead

title: Unexpectedly good
body:
I’m one of the lucky Beta version users and loved testing the app. I’ve read the Atomic Habits book several times and have successfully implemented some pretty big habits based on the book alone. So when I heard about the app I was curious because I was in a bit of a slump again. 
I didn't expect it but the app really worked for me. I've stuck with it for 28 days, and I'm working on 3 habits with great results.
I agree that the price tag of £119 per year seems like a lot. I was going to stop or stay on the free plan but those 3 habits are just too good and it works for me. I think that the benefits I'll get from my new habits over a year will far outweigh the cost, so I'm in.
